summary: This diff adds four new deterministic audit-pipeline scripts (data-model, product-quality, documentation, and a phase close-out script) plus supporting config (ai-os/.sqlfluff, an ESLint ISO-25010 ruleset, and the phase plan YAML) -- all net-new tooling files that write findings into the existing shared audit_findings/audit_runs sqlite tables, with no changes to production application code, CI/CD workflows, migrations, schema files, or auth/permission logic, so the pre-classified tier1 (additive, low-blast-radius) label is correct. Subprocess calls consistently use list-form args (no shell=True), sqlite writes are fully parameterized (no SQL injection), and a cross-process fcntl write-lock guards the shared DB matching the established sibling-pipeline convention. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. A few non-blocking quality issues surfaced: the rls_presence check in audit_pipeline_data_model.py does raw regex matching over whole-file text without stripping SQL comments, so a commented-out 'ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' statement would produce a false negative and silently suppress a genuine missing-RLS finding; audit_pipeline_documentation.py imports shutil but never appears to use it; and run_prisma_validate invokes 'npx --yes prisma validate' rather than the repo-local node_modules/.bin binary the way the sibling eslint pipeline deliberately does, which is a minor inconsistency and a soft supply-chain/version-pinning concern. The diff payload supplied for review was also truncated before showing the actual contents of ai-os/.sqlfluff, ai-os/AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-24.yaml, and the ESLint ruleset .mjs file, so those three files could not be directly inspected even though they appear in the diffstat. None of these issues are severe enough to block an additive, non-production audit-tooling change whose worst-case failure mode is an incomplete or missed finding rather than a broken build or security regression.
issues: rls_presence regex check in audit_pipeline_data_model.py does not strip SQL comments before matching ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, risking false negatives (missed high-severity RLS findings) if a migration contains a commented-out ALTER TABLE statement
audit_pipeline_documentation.py imports shutil but does not appear to use it

run_prisma_validate uses bare 'npx --yes prisma validate' instead of a repo-local pinned binary, inconsistent with the eslint pipeline's deliberate use of node_modules/.bin/eslint and a soft supply-chain/version-pinning concern
